change_log: 1.1 floors set from our baselines (min_member_accuracy 0.66 = the best a member gets alone at its weakest, Pinecrest local-only 0.662; gap 0.08 = about twice the plain FedAvg gap 0.042); personalization clause added after experiment E5 showed Harbor's reversed lives_alone effect (docs/model_card.md); DP 0.3 kept because DP 1.0 fails the member floor (E6)
coordinator: Lakeshore General Health IT (rotates annually under the charter)
approved_by: Consortium Steering Committee (one seat per member, one patient representative)
evaluation_set: neutral_eval.csv: 400 consented, de-identified rows from each member's population, tagged by member, held by the coordinator for evaluation only

personalization.why: Harbor pairs patients who live alone with a visiting nurse, so lives_alone lowers risk there and raises it everywhere else. One shared weight cannot fit both. A member may fine-tune the shared model on its own rows for 3 epochs and use that version for its own patients when it beats the shared model on its neutral slice by 0.02 or more. Fine-tuning happens inside the member; no rows move.
